scene: Child: (focused intently on the tablet, interacting with it)
Parent: Now, if I can take the tablet back [inaudible 00:00:08].
Child: (continues looking at the tablet)
Parent: Alright, thank you so much for your patience. Okay, let's take this now.
Child: (sitting with the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: Alrighty, you can start.
Child: (slightly nods)
Child: (holds the tablet, looking at the parent)
Parent: This is the book you want to read? We read this one before.
Child: (nods and says eagerly) Yeah, I want to read it again.
Child: (ready and focused on the tablet)
Parent: We can repeat the same book?
Child: (smiling) Yeah, sure.
Child: (sitting upright, looking at the parent)
Parent: Okay, so what's the name of the book?
Child: (looking at the tablet, hand on the tablet)
Parent: The bad...
Child: (still looking at the tablet, concentrating)
Parent: A Bad Case-
Child: (focused on the tablet)
Parent: Of.
Child: (maintains focus on the tablet, begins to smile slightly)
Parent: Of Stripes by David Shannon. Do you want to read by yourself a little bit? Not right now? But you can help me out okay.
Child: (nods slightly, maintaining focus on the tablet)
Parent: Okay.
Child: (looking at the tablet, attentive)
Parent: Camilla Cream loved lima beans, but-
Child: (corrects pronunciation)
Parent: Lima.
Child: (smiles, looking at the tablet)

Parent: Lima beans. But she never eat them. All of her friends hated lima beans and she wanted to fit in. Camilla was always worried about what other people thought of her. Today she was fretting even more than usual. It was the first day of school and she couldn't decide what to wear. There were so many people to impress. She tried on 42 outfits.
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: (reading) "How many outfits?"
Child: (excitedly responds, looking at parent) "Three billions, thousand, million, infinity."
Parent: (smiling, reading the tablet) "42 outfits."
Child: (insisting) "No, she tried out infinity, billion."
Parent: (gently points at the tablet) "Concentrate here."
Child: (leans closer, smiles)
Parent: (continues reading) "But none seemed quite right. She put on pretty red dress and looked in the mirror. Then she screamed."
Child: (looking at the tablet, focused)
Child: (looking at parent, smiling)
Parent: "What happened? That's the way people scream?"
Child: (smiling and looking at the tablet)
Parent: "I think the way people scream."
Child: "Okay."
Child: (looking at the parent)
Parent: "That's the way people scream."
Child: (leans forward, looking more closely at the tablet)
Child: (looks back at the tablet)
Parent: "Her mother went into the room and she screamed too. "Oh my heavens." She cried. "You are completely covered with stripes."
Child: (listening attentively)
Child: (sits up straight, watching the tablet)
Parent: "This was certainly true. Camilla was striped from head to toe. She looked like a rainbow."
Child: (sitting beside the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: Is this true? Is this in real life?
Child: (turns towards the parent and raises a hand, seeming curious)
Parent: I think this is an imagination. What do you think?
Child: (leans closer to the tablet, attentive)
Parent: Real life? Oh my God. Let's see.
Child: (stands up from the chair, leaning over the tablet)
Parent: So she looked like a rainbow. Mrs. Cream felt Camilla's forehead. "Do you feel all right?" She asked.
Child: (continues looking at the tablet, interested)
Parent: "I feel fine," Camilla answered. "But just look at me."
Parent: "You get back in bed this instant." Her mother ordered.
Parent: "You are not going to school today."
Parent: Camilla was relieved. She didn't want to miss the first day of school, but she was afraid of what the other kids would say.
Parent: And she had no idea what to wear with those crazy stripes.
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: What do you think? Oh my goodness.
Child: (leans closer to the tablet)
Parent: Her tummy is even rainbow. Oh my goodness. [inaudible 00:04:33]. Sit properly, sit properly.
Child: (leans back into the chair, turning slightly to look at the parent)

Parent: That afternoon, Dr. Bumble came to examine Camilla. "Most extraordinary," he exclaimed. "I have never seen anything like it. Are you having any coughing, sneezing, runny nose, aches, pains, chills, hot flashes, dizziness, drowsiness."
Child: (touches the parent's shoulder, looking a bit impatient)
Parent: What? Why can't you just read quick?
Child: (leaning back slightly, looking at the tablet)

Parent: Uncontrollable twitching? "No," Camilla told him. "I feel fine." "Well then," Dr. Bumble said, turning to Mrs. Cream. "I don't see any reason why she shouldn't go to school tomorrow. Here is some ointment that should help clear up those stripes in a few days. If it doesn't, you know where to reach me." And off he went. The next day was a disaster. Everyone at school laughed at Camilla. They called her Camilla Crayon and Night of the Living Lollipop. She tried her best to act as if everything were normal, but when the class said the pledge of allegiance, her stripes turned red, white, and blue and she broke down in tears.
Child: (looking at the tablet attentively)
Parent: "Oh, her color changes."
Child: (still looking at the tablet)
Parent: "I know."
Child: (reaching towards the tablet, potentially interacting with it)
Parent: "Do you know what... Can you guess anything?"
Child: (sitting back, expressing curiosity)

Parent: "The other kids thought this was great. One yelled out, "let's see some purple polka dots." Sure enough, Camilla turned all purple polka-dotty. Someone else shouted, "checkerboard!" And a pattern of squares covered her skin. Soon everyone was calling out different shapes and colors and poor Camilla was changing faster than you can change channels on a TV."
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: Can we imagine? What can happen. Oh my goodness.
Child: (still looking at the tablet)

Parent: That night, Mrs. Harms, the school principal, called. "I am sorry, Mrs. Cream,” he said. "I’m going to have to ask you to keep Camilla home from school. She’s just too much of a distraction, and I’ve been getting calls from the other parents. They’re afraid those stripes may be contagious.”
Child: (starts to lean closer to the parent)
Parent: Do you know what is mean by contagious?
Child: (shakes head)
Parent: No.
Child: (leans even closer to the parent, looking up)
Parent: Do you know?
Child: (shakes head again)

Parent: No. Contagious means if you have it. If I'm with you, maybe I can catch it too. Thank you, thank you. Sit. so if you touch me, you will get my disease. Like when we cough in front of other people, they will have cold and cough.
Child: (looks at the parent attentively while the parent explains)
Child: (reaching out and touching the parent's back)
Parent: "What if I touch your back? Wait, why I ever get back pain when I touch you?"
Child: (still holding onto the parent's shoulder and seems attentive)

Parent: "No, no. Those are not contagious. Contagious is when you touch... With the touch from skin to skin, those viruses can go from one body to another body, like the skin problem maybe. Yes, it is contagious, but when you have pain in your bone or muscle, it's not contagious. Understand?"
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Parent: "You have a pain in your bone."
Child: (leans over the tablet, looking at the screen closely)
Parent: "Yeah. It's not contagious."
Child: (listening to the parent and looking at the tablet)

Parent: "Camilla was so embarrassed. She couldn’t believe that two days ago everyone liked her. Now, nobody wanted to be in the same room with her. Her father tried to make her feel better. 'Is there anything I can get you, sweetheart?' He asked. 'No, thank you,' sighed Camilla. What she really wanted was a nice plate of lima beans, but she had been laughed at enough for one day."
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the tablet)

Parent: "Hmm well, yes, I see, Dr. Bumble" mumbled when Mr. Cream phoned the next day. "I think I’d better bring in the specialists. We'll be right over.” About an hour later, Dr. Bumble arrived with four people in long white coats. He introduced them to the Creams. "This is Dr. Grop, Dr. Sponge, Dr. Cricket, and Dr. Young." Then the specialists went to work to Camilla. They squeezed and jabbed, tapped and tested. It was very uncomfortable."
Child: (looking at the tablet, listening attentively)

Parent: "Well. It is not the mumps," concluded Dr. Grop. "Or the measles," said Dr. Sponge. "Definitely not chicken pox," put in Dr. Cricket. "Or sunburn," said Dr. Young. "Try these," said the Specialists. They each handed her a bottle filled with different colored pills. Take one of each before bed, said Dr. Grop. Then they filed out the front door, followed by Dr. Bumble."
Child: (leans in closer to the tablet, looking curious)
Parent: Field or filed. Oh my goodness. What is this? Can you imagine? Poor Camilla.
Child: (slightly moves closer to the tablet, still focused)

Parent: That night, Camilla took her medicine. It was awful. When she woke up the next morning, she did feel different, but when she got dressed, her clothes didn’t fit her right. She looked in the mirror, and there, staring back at her, was a giant, multi-colored pill with her face on it. Dr. Bumble rushed over as soon as Mrs. Cream called, but this time instead of the specialist, he brought the experts.
Child: (maintains focus on the tablet)
Parent: (points at the tablet) Can you read one or two words?
Child: No. (appears unsure)
Child: (still looking at the tablet, listens intently)

Parent: Dr. Gourd and Mr. Mellon were the finest scientific minds in the land. Once again, Camilla was poked and prodded, looked at and listened to. The experts wrote down lots of numbers. Then they huddled together and whispered. Dr. Gourd finally spoke. "It might be a virus," he announced with authority. Suddenly, fuzzy little virus balls appeared all over Camilla. "Or possibly some form of bacteria," said Mr. Mellon. Out popped squiggly little bacteria tails. "Or it could be a fungus," added Dr. Gourd. Instantly, Camilla was covered with different colored fungus blotches.
Child: (sitting next to the parent, looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Oh my goodness."
Child: (continues looking at the tablet)
Child: (still looking at the tablet)

Parent: "The Experts looked at Camilla, then at each other. 'We need to go over these numbers again back at the lab,' Dr. Gourd explained. 'We will call you when we know something.' But the experts didn’t have a clue, much less a cure."
Child: (remains focused on the tablet)
Child: (begins to reach towards the tablet)
Parent: "Oh yeah."
Child: (touches the tablet)
Child: (sitting back slightly but still engaged, looking at the parent)

Parent: "By now, [inaudible 00:13:50] the T.V. news had found out about Camilla. Reporters from every channel were outside her house, telling the story of The Bizarre Case of the Incredible Changing Kid. Soon a huge crowd was camped out on the front lawn."
Child: (looks back at the tablet)
Child: (leaning in, looking at the tablet)
Parent: "Oh my goodness, what is this?"
Child: (continues looking at the tablet)
Child: (focuses on listening to the parent, slightly turning towards them)
Parent: "The Creams were swamped with all kinds of remedies from psychologists, allergists, herbalists, nutritionists, psychics-"
Child: (looking back at the tablet, staying close to the parent)
Parent: "She is a very, very-"
Child: (leans in closer to the tablet)
Parent: "An old medicine man, a guru, and even-"
Child: (looks up at the parent, seeming curious)
Parent: "A grew a cow?"
Child: (leaning in, engaged with the parent)
Parent: "No, guru means an expert."
Child: (points at the tablet, appears very focused)
Parent: "No guru means cow in Bangla."
Child: (listening intently, not moving)
Parent: "Bangla, guru means cow, but over here a guru means an expert."
Child: (looks up at parent and seems to repeat the word)
Parent: "A [Bu-ru 00:14:55]."
Child: (continuing to listen to the story)
Parent: "And even a veterinarian. Each so-called cure only added to poor Camilla’s strange appearance until it was hard to even recognize her. She sprouted roots and berries and crystals..."
Child: (sitting beside the parent, looking at the tablet screen)
Parent: Where are the crystals, can you see?
Child: (points at the tablet screen) There.
Parent: Where?
Child: (continues pointing at multiple spots on the screen) There and there.
Parent: Crystals.
Child: (points again at the tablet screen) There and there and there.

Parent: (reads from storybook) Oh my goodness. Oh yes. And feathers and a long furry tail. But nothing worked. One day, a woman who called herself an environmental therapist claimed she could cure Camilla. "Close your eyes," she said.
Child: (slouching, leaning forward, not sitting properly)
Parent: "[foreign language 00:15:51]. Sit properly [inaudible 00:15:53]. Nicely, thank you."
Child: (still leaning forward but trying to sit more properly)
Parent: "And she said 'breathe deeply, and become one with your room.'"
Child: (looking at the parent with curiosity)
Parent: ""I wish you hadn't said that," Camilla groaned. Slowly, she started to melt into the walls of her room. Her bed became her mouth, her nose was a dresser, and two paintings were her eyes."
Child: (points to the screen, specifically focusing on the dresser)
Parent: "Where's her dresser? Oh."
Child: (pointing back to the screen, looks slightly confused)
Parent: "The therapist screamed and ran from the house."
Child: (standing up and facing away from the parent and the book)
Parent: Is that... Okay, okay, okay. Let's read the rest of the book. Okay, come back.
Child: (walking back towards the parent)
Child: (standing near the chair beside the parent)
Parent: Everything they say I'm...
Child: (moving to stand on the other side of the parent)
Child: (leaning towards the tablet next to the parent)
Parent: "What are we going to do?”
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Child: (standing up straight after looking at the tablet)
Parent: What are we going to do?
Child: (standing beside the parent)
Child: (leaning towards the tablet again)
Parent: "Cried Mrs. Cream. “It just keeps -”
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Child: (leaning further towards the tablet)
Parent: "Cried Mrs. Cream."
Child: (continuing to look at the tablet)
Child: (standing up straight and moving slightly away from the tablet)
Parent: "It just keeps getting worse and worse!" She began to sob.
Child: (standing beside the parent)
Child: (leaning slightly closer to the tablet again, with one hand on the table)
Parent: It just keeps getting worse and worse.
Child: (looking at the tablet)
Child: (standing up and moving the chair slightly)

Parent: At that moment, Mrs. Cream heard a quiet little knock at the front door. He opened it, and there stood an old woman who was just as plump and sweet as a strawberry. "Excuse me," she said brightly.
Child: (standing next to the chair, facing the parent and the tablet)
Child: (standing beside the parent, looking at the parent's hand)
Parent: Actually, stay seated please.
Child: (moving to sit down but still partially standing)
Parent: Sit down.
Child: (looking at the parent, concerned)
Parent: The cameras won't catch you.
Child: (continues to look at the parent with concern)
Parent: Okay. So you have to sit down or the cameras will catch you. They're set for a specific spot.
Child: No they're going to catch me. They're going to catch me.
Parent: Listen to the end. It's almost done.
Child: (sitting down next to the parent, leaning in)
Parent: "Excuse me," she said brightly. "But I think I can help."
Child: (sitting on the chair, looking at the parent)
Parent: "Excuse me."
Child: (continues looking at the parent and the tablet)
Child: (sitting on the chair, looking at the parent)
Parent: "Do you think she can help?"
Child: (continues looking at the tablet)
Child: (sitting on the chair, continues looking at the parent)
Parent: "Excuse me, I think I can help."
Child: (looks at the tablet, paying attention)
Child: (starts looking around, not focusing on the tablet)
Parent: "Do you think she can help? Let's see."
Child: (glances at the tablet again)
Child: (sitting back, paying attention to the parent and the tablet)

Parent: "She went into Camilla’s room and looked around. 'My goodness,' she said with a shake of her head. 'What we have here is a bad case of stripes. One of the worst I have ever seen!' She pulled a container of small green beans from her bag. 'Here,' she said. 'These might do the trick.'"
Child: (attentively listening and looking at the tablet)
Child: (leaning over the tablet, looking at the screen)
Parent: "Oh my goodness, what are these?"
Child: (continuing to look at the screen of the tablet)
Parent: "They are lima beans."
Child: (hands poised, ready to touch the screen of the tablet)
Parent: (pointing at the screen) "Are those magic beans?" asked Mrs. Cream.
Child: (hands relaxed on the table, still looking at the screen)
Parent: “Oh my, no,” replied the kind old woman. “There is no such thing. These are just plain old lima beans. I'll bet you’d like some, wouldn’t you?” she asked Camilla.
Child: (looking intently at the screen)
Parent: Camilla wanted a big, heaping plateful of lima beans more than just about anything, but she was still afraid to admit it. “Yuck!” she said.
Child: (appears to smile, showing interest)
Parent: “No one likes lima beans, especially me!” “Oh, dear,” the old woman said sadly. “I guess I was wrong about you.” She put the beans back in her bag and started toward the door.
Child: (still focused on the tablet screen)
Parent: Camilla watched the old woman walk away. Those beans would taste so good. And being laughed at for eating them was nothing, compared to what she’d been going through.
Child: (looking at the tablet, focused on the story)

Parent: "She finally couldn’t stand it. “Wait!” she cried. “The truth is…I really love lima beans.” “I thought so,” the old woman said with a smile. She took a handful of beans and popped them into Camilla’s mouth. “Mmmm,” said Camilla. Suddenly the branches, feathers, and squiggly tails began to disappear. Then the whole room swirled around. When it stopped, there stood Camilla. And everything was back to normal. “I’m cured!” she shouted. “Yes,” said the old woman."
Child: (smiling, turns towards the parent)
Parent: "Yes."
Child: (speaking, "I knew the real")
Parent: "I knew the real-"
Child: (energetic, says "I'm cured! Yes!")
Parent: (continues to read) "[inaudible 00:20:46] "I knew the real you was in here somewhere.” She patted Camilla on the head. Then she went outside and vanished into the crowd."
Child: (not visible in the frame, possibly off to the side or behind the table)
Parent: What happened? You cannot go.
Child: (still not visible in the frame)
Parent: (speaking) [inaudible 00:21:09]. Really you have to sit.
Child: (appears in the background, walking to the side)
Parent: I went outside.
Child: (still in the background, moving closer to the table)
Parent: And then Camilla is coming back.
Child: (absent, not looking at the parent or the book)
Parent: [inaudible 00:21:15].
Child: (still absent)
Parent: Okay, then-
Child: (still absent)
Parent: Can we just wrap up the meeting session?
Child: (enters the scene, walking towards the parent)
Parent: Baba, come back.
Child: (sits next to the parent)

Parent: Afterward, Camilla wasn’t quite the same. Some of the kids at school said she was weird, but she didn’t care a bit. She ate all the lima beans she wanted, and she never had even a touch of stripes again.
Child: (leans in closer to the tablet, looking at it)
Parent: The end.
Child: (reaches to take the tablet)
Parent: Now, take my iPad back.
Child: (takes the tablet)
